Alright, the last few actions were all about confirming that the new “greeting” behavior is working as intended. I updated the prompts to make casual greetings get a short, friendly reply without any tool sweeps, then I rebuilt the TypeScript project (no errors) and ran a tmux smoke test of the TUI. 

The smoke test started a new tmux session called **glinttest**, launched the dev server, waited a bit, and captured the initial pane. The output showed the status line:

```
compound · effort ultracode · ctx 0 · 0 tok · $0.00 · safe · diag on · /help
```

Next I sent the string `hi` followed by an Enter key:

```bash
tmux send-keys -t glinttest 'hi' Enter && sleep 12 && tmux capture-pane -t glinttest -p | tail -25
```

The captured pane still only displayed the prompt line with `hi` and the same status bar—no friendly reply appeared. Since the UI is supposed to give a brief response to a greeting, something isn’t being triggered. 

I suspect the issue is that the input line isn’t actually being submitted to the agent yet. In many REPL‑style interfaces, typing a line and hitting Enter adds the line to the history but the actual processing occurs only after a **second** Enter (i.e., submitting an empty line). My earlier command sent `hi` **and** an Enter, but perhaps the first Enter just moved the cursor to a new line without committing the input; the UI might be waiting for an explicit “submit” action, which in this terminal UI is just a blank Enter.

To test this hypothesis I need to send a bare Enter key to the tm

arguments.command: tmux send-keys -t glinttest Enter && sleep 3 && tmux capture-pane -t glinttest -p | grep -v '^$' | tail -15
